L1_p09: Medical Terminology definition It is the language used to precisely describe the human body including its components, processes, conditions affecting it, and procedures performed upon it.  Medical terminology is used in the field of medicine and pharmacy.
L1_p10: Most medical terms are a combination of word parts prefix Root Suffix /Stem Most of them comes from Latin or Greek words Other language such as English ,German and French
L1_p11: prefix Root Suffix Root the word part that is the core of the word Prefix a word part attached to the beginning of a word root to modify its meaning Suffix a word part attached to the end of the word root to modify its meaning
L1_p12: prefix Root Suffix Combining Vowel a word part, usually an “O” or “i”
L1_p13: Carcinogen Carcin gen + Root Suffix carcin/o/gen O + Combining Vowel Producing Cancer Substance that promotes the formation of cancer

L2_p06: [ o ] is the most common combining vowel [ i ] is the second most common combining vowel. When a medical term has more than one root, each is joined by a vowel They are used to join: i – root to root. ii- root to suffix Combining vowels
L2_p07: Additional Roots {often a medical term is formed of two or more roots} Hyper/lip/o/protein/emia Root Suffix prefix Root vowel A condition of excessive fat and protein in blood Hyperlipoproteinemia
L2_p08: Why we use Combining vowels To ease pronunciation Is their presence mandatory Not all medical terms have combining vowels
L2_p09: Rules for Forming and Spelling Medical Terms 1. Memorizing and spelling basic medical word components are the first steps for learning how to form medical terms 2. The next step is to construct the words using the following steps
L2_p10: 1-A combing vowel is used to join root to root as well as to any suffix beginning with a constant Electr cardi gram + + Root Root Suffix Electric Record Electr/o/cardi/o/gram Electrical record of the heart Heart
L2_p12: 2-A combining vowel is not used before a suffix that begins with a vowel
L2_p13: 2-A combining vowel is not used before a suffix that begins with a vowel Vas Ectomy + Root Suffix Vessel excision Excision of a vessel اﺳﺗﺋﺻﺎل Vasectomy
L2_p14: 3-If the roots ends in a vowel and the suffix begins with the same vowel, drop the final vowel from the root and do not use a combining vowel Inflammation of heart Heart cardi itis + Inflammation Carditis
L2_p15: Intestine 4- when a prefix ends in a vowel and the root begins with a vowel, the final vowel is dropped from the prefix para enter al + + prefix Root Suffix Alongside of Pertaining to Pertaining to alongside of the intestine Parenteral
L2_p16: 4-Most often a combining vowel is inserted between two roots even when the second root begins with a vowel. Cardi esophag eal Root Root Suffix cardi/o/esophag/eal pertaining to heart and esophagus Pertaining to Heart
L2_p17: Formation of medical terms • All medical terms build from the root. • Prefixes and suffixes are attached to the root to modify its meaning . • Often two or more roots are linked before being modified.
